prompt: A streaming service charges a $\$12$ sign-up fee plus $\$8$ per month. A rival charges no fee but $\$10$ per month. After how many months have you paid the same total on both?
hint: Write an expression for the total paid to each service after $m$ months, then think about what "the same total" means.

hints.text: Write an expression for the total paid to each service after $m$ months, then think about what "the same total" means.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Test month $1$: $12 + 8 = \$20$ versus the rival. Keep testing months, or set both cost expressions equal.
Set the totals equal: $12 + 8m = 10m$. Subtract $8m$ from both sides to get $12 = 2m$.
$12 \div 2 = 6$, so the totals match after $6$ months, when each is $60$ dollars.

explanation: The first service costs $12 + 8m$ and the rival costs $10m$, so equal totals means $12 + 8m = 10m$.
Subtract $8m$ from both sides to get $12 = 2m$, then divide by $2$ to get $m = 6$.
Check: $12 + 48 = 60$ and $10 \times 6 = 60$, so the totals are the same after $6$ months.

alternativeExplanations.title: Gap-closing story
steps: The fee puts you $12 behind on service one from day zero. But each month it charges $2 LESS than the rival.
Saving $2 a month erases a $12 head start in 12 ÷ 2 = 6 months.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a table
steps: Month 2: fee plan = 28, rival = 20. Month 4: 44 vs 40. Month 6: 60 vs 60.
